description: Behavioral Evaluation: STAR Methodology & Engineering Conflict Resolution

prompts.statement: Tell me about a time when you had a fundamental technical disagreement with a team member or mentor regarding the architecture or implementation approach for a critical deliverable. How did you handle the disagreement, what evidence or prototypes did you use to evaluate options, and what was the ultimate outcome?
constraints: Structure response using the STAR framework (Situation, Task, Action, Result)
Focus on technical merits and data-driven evaluation rather than interpersonal tension
Articulate specific trade-offs and retrospective lessons learned

examples.input: Disagreement on ORM versus raw SQL queries under tight production latencies
examples.expected: Built a side-by-side benchmark harness simulating 1,000 req/s, demonstrated 4x latency reduction and predictable query plans, aligned team on a hybrid approach.

clarificationBranches.question: Can the outcome be one where my preferred approach was NOT chosen?
clarificationBranches.answer: Yes. Demonstrating 'disagree and commit' with objective post-launch monitoring is viewed favorably.

followups.question: Looking back, what is one thing you would do differently in how you communicated the technical trade-offs?
followups.criterion: Demonstrates self-awareness and prioritizes empathy and early alignment over being proven right.

privateReference.approach: Evaluate candidate on 4 dimensions: (1) Constructive framing without blame, (2) Grounding in empirical data or reproducible prototypes, (3) Professional alignment and execution discipline, (4) Honest reflection on lessons learned.
checks: Covers all 4 STAR components within 4 minutes
Shows ownership and bias for action
privateReference.expectedComplexity: High signal on emotional intelligence and technical maturity

packs.title: Behavioral Evaluation: Technical Disagreement & STAR
packs.instructions: Simulated live behavioral interview. Deliver a concise, evidence-driven STAR narrative demonstrating leadership, technical conviction, and collaboration.
